Preparation tips:

• Raise furniture, electrical devices and valuables.
• Install barriers or protection systems.
• Check domestic sump pumps.
• Prepare an emergency kit (boots, torches, batteries, documents).
• Monitor notifications and forecasts via the app.
• Avoid leaving vehicles in risky areas.

Behaviors to reduce risks:

• Avoid walking in deep water or unlit areas.
• Beware of electrical cables, open manholes or hidden obstacles.
• Use only authorized walkways.
• Do not force doors or accesses under strong water pressure.
• Limit the use of vehicles.
• Wear high boots or waterproof protection.

Guidelines for returning to normality:

• Avoid switching on electrical appliances until dry and checked.
• Clean and disinfect premises and surfaces contaminated by brackish water.
• Properly dispose of damaged goods.
• Report structural damage to competent offices.
• Document damages for insurance claims.

The chart shows the astronomical tide trend day by day.

On the horizontal axis the hours of the day are shown (0–24), while on the vertical axis the tide height in centimeters relative to the sea zero is reported.

The blue line represents the sea level:

 • Peaks indicate high tides

 • Lowest points indicate low tides

Next to the maxima and minima the following are reported:

 • Time

 • Predicted tide height

Moon symbols indicate the lunar phases:

 • Full and new moon → stronger tides

 • First and last quarter → milder tides

From September 15 to April 30 the City Administration, based on forecasts issued by the Tide Center, activates the Pedestrian Viability Plan on walkways managed and installed by the company VERITAS SpA. During this period, high water is more likely to occur in Venice. The routes indicated on the map ensure dry foot passage up to a tide level of +120 cm. Above this level some routes may become impassable.

The MOSE (Electromechanical Experimental Module) is an integrated defense system made up of rows of mobile retractable barriers, installed at the lagoon entrances of Lido, Malamocco and Chioggia, capable of temporarily isolating the Venice lagoon from the Adriatic Sea during high tide events.

The mobile barriers are normally submerged and filled with water. When a high tide is forecast, compressed air is injected into the barriers so that, emptied of water, they rise by rotating around a hinge fixed to the seabed. Once raised, the barriers form a barrier that separates the lagoon from the sea, preventing high water from entering.

MOSE is activated when a tide higher than 110 cm above mean sea level is forecast. The decision to activate the system is taken by the Tide Forecast and Reporting Center of the Municipality of Venice, based on weather-marine forecasts. Activation requires about 4–5 hours notice and the system may remain raised for several hours depending on the event.

• 78 mobile barriers divided among the 3 lagoon entrances
• Barrier dimensions: up to 30 meters wide, 20 high
• Weight: about 300 tons per barrier
• Installation depth: between 10 and 30 meters
• Raising time: about 30 minutes
• Capacity: defense up to 3 meters of tide
